charts.title: Final computer-use accuracy
charts.description: Model 2 clearly outperformed both JEPA-transfer models.

charts.title: What SFT added to each starting point
charts.description: SFT helped all models, but it did not repair the large JEPA transfer loss.

charts.title: Final policy metric profile
charts.description: All models produced valid JSON, but the JEPA models often chose the wrong action or location.

charts.title: Click precision at three tolerances
charts.description: Model 2 found screen locations much more accurately at every tolerance.

charts.title: Final quality by GUI action type
charts.description: Click dominates the dataset. Rare-action scores are unstable because their sample counts are small.

charts.title: Did the model choose the correct kind of action?
charts.description: Model 2 was strongest overall. All models were weak on several rare actions.

charts.title: Final policy score by operating system
charts.description: Model 2 led on macOS, Ubuntu, and Windows.

charts.title: Final policy score by software domain
charts.description: The right panel shows sample size so that small-domain results are not mistaken for stable estimates.

charts.title: Which actions were confused?
charts.description: Rows are the correct actions. Columns are the model outputs. Values are percentages within each row.

charts.title: Distribution of final per-example scores
charts.description: Model 2 produced many more fully correct actions.

charts.title: Coordinate error distribution when the action type was correct
charts.description: The Model 2 curve rises earlier, which means its predicted locations were closer to the targets.

charts.title: Small live-monitor trajectory
charts.description: This monitor was easier than the full validation set. It is a health signal, not the final result.

charts.title: SFT training loss
charts.description: Model 2 had the lowest overall training loss. Curves use a five-record moving average.

charts.title: Loss reduction during SFT
charts.description: All models learned the supervised format, but lower training loss did not remove the JEPA transfer gap.

charts.title: Visual and language LoRA gradient norms
charts.description: Both adapter parts received gradients throughout training. The poor JEPA result was not caused by zero gradients.

charts.title: Matched SFT learning-rate schedule
charts.description: The three runs used the same warmup and cosine decay schedule.

charts.title: SFT GPU memory use
charts.description: Each full SFT run peaked at 13.84 GiB on a 24 GiB L4 GPU.

charts.title: SFT time, cost, and peak GPU memory
charts.description: Resource use was almost equal, which supports the fairness of the model comparison.

charts.title: Trainable SFT parameter allocation
charts.description: All three models trained the same number of adapter parameters. Base Qwen parameters were frozen.

charts.title: Training difficulty by action type
charts.description: Writing and rare actions were often harder than ordinary clicks.

charts.title: Paired wins and ties on the same 250 examples
charts.description: Most Model 3 versus Model 4 examples were ties. Model 2 had many more wins against both.

charts.title: Where final policy errors came from
charts.description: All outputs parsed. The main failures were wrong action types and wrong action details.

charts.title: Action distribution in the SFT data
charts.description: Clicks were 65% of training data. Scroll had only 6 training and 2 validation examples.

charts.title: Operating-system balance
charts.description: Train and validation data were nearly equal across macOS, Ubuntu, and Windows.

charts.title: Largest software domains in the SFT data
charts.description: The data covered many domains, but the distribution was not uniform.

charts.title: Sampling rate by action type
charts.description: Rare actions were sampled more heavily than clicks, but some still had very small absolute counts.

charts.title: Dataset integrity checks
charts.description: The saved SFT dataset had no missing images, duplicates, or exact split overlap.

charts.title: What JEPA training changed
charts.description: Action-conditioned Model 4 improved future matching. The no-action control remained at chance.

charts.title: JEPA future-screen accuracy over training
charts.description: Only the action-conditioned model moved clearly above chance.

charts.title: JEPA training losses
charts.description: Both runs reduced latent regression loss. Model 4 also optimized action separation.

charts.title: JEPA objective components
charts.description: Model 3 correctly had zero action-separation loss. Model 4 paid a large action-separation term.

charts.title: How much correct action information helped JEPA prediction
charts.description: A positive gap means correct actions produced closer predictions. Model 4 developed a small positive gap.

charts.title: Target and predicted representation variance
charts.description: Model 4's final predicted variance was very small even though target variance remained substantial.

charts.title: JEPA accuracy by amount of screen change
charts.description: Action-conditioned performance varied strongly with how much of the screen changed.

charts.title: JEPA runtime by phase
charts.description: Training dominated the JEPA wall time. Final evaluation was the next largest phase.

charts.title: JEPA resource use
charts.description: The matched no-action and action-conditioned Qwen JEPA runs used similar resources.

charts.title: JEPA adapter and head parameter composition
charts.description: The two JEPA controls had matched parameter counts. The full Qwen base remained frozen.

charts.title: JEPA architecture search results
charts.description: Grey same-app diagnostics used an easier test and are not directly comparable with held-out-app runs.

charts.title: Variation across repeated V-JEPA pilot seeds
charts.description: Dots are individual seeds. Orange lines are two-seed means. Two seeds are still too few for a stable estimate.

charts.title: Where action-conditioned JEPA lost or gained against Model 2
charts.description: Model 4 lost most heavily on clicks. Tiny positive values on rare actions are not stable evidence.

charts.title: Core training cost per model
charts.description: This is training cost, not inference cost. Inference latency and cost were not measured.
sources: JEPA and SFT final_metrics cost estimates

charts.title: How each model reached its final policy score
charts.description: The higher Model 4 JEPA score did not transfer into a better computer-use policy.

charts.title: Which parts of the original thesis were tested?
charts.description: The MVP tested accuracy and action conditioning. It did not yet test inference cost or annotation cost.

charts.title: GPU memory and allocated host RAM
charts.description: GPU memory was measured. Host RAM is the Modal allocation, not measured resident usage.
sources: JEPA/SFT metrics and Modal function settings

charts.title: Action mix in the synthetic JEPA data
charts.description: Clicks dominate both splits. Typing and scrolling supply smaller action groups.

charts.title: Applications used for JEPA training and validation
charts.description: Jira and Slack were held out from JEPA training. This tests transfer to unseen applications.

charts.title: How much each action changed the screen
charts.description: Validation actions changed more of the screen on average than training actions.

charts.title: Synthetic JEPA data used by the full runs
charts.description: Both full JEPA runs used 30,668 training transitions and 2,000 validation transitions.

charts.title: JEPA train and validation split checks
charts.description: The split prevents exact screen reuse and holds out two complete applications.
